§C.13 The Ground-Truth File

Procedure

The deliverable for a chart page is its {name}.test.json: chart_data_point rules, one per data point, covering every data point in the chart (Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1) — plus a chart_judge_point rule for each fact no printed text locates or no single table shape carries: whisker spans, choropleth classes, gantt spans, sankey flows.

The files on disk

File What it is
{name}.pdf the single page holding the chart — the only source of truth
{name}.test.json the ground truth — the file you deliver
{name}_llama_agentic.md a reference parse, roughly 70–80% right — reference only, never authority

The JSON envelope has three keys: expected_markdown (stays null), test_rules, and tags. The top-level tags carry document provenance from the fixed sector vocabulary (domain:government, domain:energy, …); the loader copies them onto every rule.

The rule

One rule = one data point:

{
  "type": "chart_data_point",
  "labels": ["Very high DSI", "2014"],
  "value": "25 (13.0%)",
  "max_diffs": 0,
  "normalize_numbers": true,
  "verified": true,
  "id": "4d47b974398b0306"
}

You author three things: labels (the printed text that locates the point — Labels§11.1.2), value (printed or estimated — Values and Tolerances§11.1.4), and relative_tolerance on estimated values only. The other fields (type, max_diffs, normalize_numbers, verified) are handled by the annotation tool, and id is stamped on save — never authored. Estimated rules also carry "tags": ["need_estimate"].

The judge rule

A few chart families carry facts no printed text locates — an error bar's whisker span, a choropleth's region-to-class pairing, a gantt bar's span on the time axis. Those get a second rule shape, scored by an LLM judge that accepts any output faithfully conveying the fact:

{
  "type": "chart_judge_point",
  "chart_type": "map_class",
  "labels": ["CO"],
  "expected": {"region": "CO", "class": "20%-<25%"},
  "verified": true
}

You author chart_type (error_bar, box_plot, map_class, gantt_span, or sankey_flow), the same labels, the family's expected payload, and a tolerance on estimated payloads. Where each applies, with worked pages: Scatter and Error Bars§11.2.8 (whiskers and box plots), Gantt and Sankey Charts§11.2.3 (task spans in one gantt_span shape, ribbon flows in one sankey_flow shape), Maps and Treemaps§11.2.7 (choropleth classes). Everything printed or axis-readable stays a chart_data_point.

The checker looks each rule up independently — it finds the value in the parsed tables and verifies the labels sit on that cell's row and column. No order matters, no orientation matters, and no rule says which chart on the page it belongs to; the labels do the locating.

In the examples across these notes, rules are shown in the short authored form — labels / value / relative_tolerance / tags — since the tool supplies the rest.
